summary: Progressive latency surge and client disconnects when requesting very large max_tokens with deep system prompt
description: Issue summary: Customer reports progressive per-token latency increase culminating in client connection resets and 499/504 errors when using very large max_tokens (120k) together with a deep multi-part system prompt (~90k tokens). Impact: production traffic for BrightGuide's document-summarization pipeline experiences 10-25% request failures during nightly batch runs; escalated by account success due to SLA. Environment: production, us-east-1, using hosted Redwood API endpoints. Steps to reproduce: 1) POST /v1/generate with model=gpt-neoxt-20b, max_tokens=120000, streaming=true. 2) Include system prompt comprised of concatenated user history + company policy (~90k token prefix). 3) Observe token output rate, latency per token, and finalization step. Expected behavior: steady per-token latency with finalization within configured 5m window; streaming connection remains open until model completes. Actual behavior: per-token latency increases nonlinearly after ~40k output tokens; streaming chunk intervals stretch from ~60ms to >2s; finalization step stalls and client connection sometimes resets at ~7-12 minutes with 499 or 504 returned. Logs/Traces: customer provided request IDs (rgx-req-11, rgx-req-17) and partial debug traces showing long queue time in finalizer stage and repeated KV eviction/rehydration events.

investigation_notes: Observed behavior appears different from single-shot 504 cases: latency ramps slowly rather than sudden finalizer timeout.
Pod metrics show sustained GPU utilization but increasing host CPU and tail-latency in kernel dispatch after long-running requests.
KV cache metrics: frequent small evictions followed by immediate rehydration (~300-800ms penalty per rehydrate) starting around output token ~40k.
Finalizer/serializer queue depth increases with each KV rehydrate cycle; finalization attempts are serialized causing streaming gaps and eventual client timeout if the connection exceeds 7 minutes.
Tokenizer overhead: incremental decoding of very long system prompt causes repeated tokenization boundary recalculations under current tokenizer caching behavior.
Hypothesis A: Kernel context switching + KV eviction/reload loop creates cumulative latency that pushes long-running streams past client-side timeouts.
Hypothesis B: Finalizer uses a global lock for flush/serialize that contends across requests when memory pressure forces frequent cache operations.
Repro steps executed on staging with a synthetic 85k token prefix reproduced the latency ramp consistently.
Logs attached to GH issue runtime#8121 showing stack traces where serializer waits on cache-mgr lock.
Related to but distinct from SUP-66388 which dealt with intermittent sync timeouts; this incident is deterministic with huge prefixes and high max_tokens.
temporary_mitigation: Advise customer to shard requests into multiple smaller generations (e.g., 4x30k) and reassemble client-side to avoid long single-stream windows.
Enable shorter client-side keepalive and exponential backoff to improve perceived availability.
Support team suggested setting max_tokens <= 30k as immediate workaround until server-side fix is deployed.
Provisioned a dedicated test pool for customer to evaluate configuration tweaks (requires customer confirmation).
resolution_notes: 2026-03-14: Deployed targeted patch to runtime repo (PR #8121) that reduces KV eviction aggressiveness for requests with large predicted output budgets and makes finalizer serialization more fine-grained.
Patched branch run in canary for 4 hours against synthetic workload; observed elimination of progressive latency ramp and no finalizer queue buildup.
Confirmed customer acceptance testing window; BrightGuide validated that previously failing requests completed successfully in canary with patched config.

Follow-ups: schedule a post-release monitoring window (48 hours) and update runbook with guidance for handling extreme max_tokens workloads. Also add telemetry to warn when predicted output > 50k tokens.
Status: awaiting production rollout approval from Ops and final sign-off from Customer Success.
